_about: Machine-readable catalogue of every Paper Cinema system. Generated from SYSTEMS.md by tools/build_systems.py; connections = [from, to] data flow.

systems.name: Lantern Origami
systems.does: The look: faceted washi paper lit from inside; amber = human, crimson = demonic; paint not blood

systems.name: Strike Grammar
systems.does: Every attack in 6 beats: ready → wind-up → slash → hit-stop → follow-through → reaction

systems.name: Film file
systems.does: One JSON per film: shots, camera, performances, duels, events, shakes, titles, sounds, format

systems.name: Checker
systems.does: Validates a film and explains every mistake in plain words

systems.name: One-command pipeline
systems.does: check → stills → render → sound → playbook

systems.name: One-command film (Blender + sound)
systems.does: `tools/film.sh film/<name>.json` → `output/<name>-final.mp4`: validate → export motion → events (auto clash/whoosh cues) → studio audit (must pass) → Blender render (four niced one-thread processes over the four cores, resumable: frames already in `output/blender/<name>/` are kept, `--from/--to` for one stretch, `--fresh` to redo them, 360x640/16 preview by default and `--full` for 720x1280/48) → encode → voice → sound and mix → a report of duration, size, LUFS and true peak. `--set <name>` stages the film in a Blender set; `--gpu` refuses with the reason (see `KAGGLEFARM`); `--reuse-motion` takes the exported motion as it stands

systems.name: Free Kaggle Blender farm
systems.does: The render job as DATA (`job.json` in a private dataset: `blender/`, `assets/models`, `library/`, the film and its motion), `run.sh pack/push/wait/get`, a 5 s heartbeat (frames, GPU, RAM, Blender's last line) so a killed kernel still says where it stopped. Broken: the kernel is cancelled 11–18 s into every render with no message; quota, GPU attachment, idle GPU, device, memory, disk, CPU quota, dataset mount, output folder, picture settings and every effect switch are measured and ruled out

systems.name: New-film scaffolder
systems.does: Signature opening + fight body + end card, vertical by default
systems.command: node engine/new-film.mjs x --jp 漢字 --en TITLE

systems.name: Preview engine
systems.does: Builds the 3D paper world per frame (`window.renderAt(t)`), deterministic

systems.name: Sets + paper
systems.does: Layered paper sea, island, coasts, sword studio; washi materials; 10 textile patterns

systems.name: Skeleton + balance
systems.does: Shared rig: two-part spine, neck, clavicles, shoulder/forearm twist, 2-axis wrists, ankles, optional glowing eyes with lids; leg IK, stance/crouch/weight, analytic arm IK (`solveArm`)

systems.name: Motion system
systems.does: Keys of "second + pose", smooth monotone curves, breathing, cloth follow-through, walk cycle; anime layer: per-joint follow-through lag, `ease` snap curves, `settle` overshoot, `drag:0` contacts

systems.name: Fight moves
systems.does: Named moves (jump-back, parry, lunge-shomen, kesa-giri, tsuki, bind, dodge, stagger…) expanded into poses

systems.name: Planted feet + weight
systems.does: Opt-in per film (`"motion": { "lockFeet": true }`): one precomputed pass over the finished motion finds ground contacts (foot height + travel speed), pins each foot to one world point for the whole contact, steps between contacts on an eased arc (a leap or a dash becomes one long arc), then solves the legs from the pinned feet — hips drop when a leg cannot reach, and the body leans and catches itself with a step when the centre of mass leaves the support polygon. Still a pure function of `t`.

systems.name: Motion capture from video
systems.does: Film a move with a phone → MediaPipe Pose Landmarker (Apache-2.0, CPU) per frame → left/right flip fix, zero-phase one-euro + Savitzky-Golay smoothing, ground contact → our channels (ry, waist/chest, shoulders + elbows by bounded IK fit, head, stance/crouch/weight, root travel, jumps) inside the joint limits → a performance key list (every frame, `--tol`, or `--keys N`) or a move (`--as-move`, relative fwd/side/turn); a film that replays it from where the phone stood; source/ours contact sheets; synthetic accuracy test on our own figure

systems.name: Reaction layer
systems.does: Fighters watch each other; delayed threat response (function react)

systems.name: Sword draw
systems.does: One blade slides out of the scabbard into the grip, hand on the hilt

systems.name: KUROKO camera
systems.does: Automatic operator: rigs (frame/orbit/track/face/anchor/blade), feels (locked/dolly/crane/handheld/torpedo), motion-reactive behaviours, look-ahead, impact punch, guards

systems.name: Keyframe camera
systems.does: Hand-made camera paths (pos/look/fov) on smooth curves + shakes

systems.name: Library
systems.does: Swords from parts, characters on one body, outfits, patterns

systems.name: Renderer
systems.does: Headless Chrome, frame by frame → MP4; `--still`, `--vertical`, `--from/--to`

systems.name: Sound pipeline
systems.does: Find (Openverse) → check (ffmpeg) → place at cue times → mix; Earshot bank cues aimed by their apex, voice lines with ducking, an 11 dB pre-hit dip in the beds and whooshes from 0.42 s to 0.06 s before every hit (so a clash stands ≥ 9 dB above what came before it), and two measured loudness passes to -14 LUFS under a -1 dBFS true peak; credits

systems.name: Blade contact + hit-stop
systems.does: Finds blade-to-blade contact (segment distance, 240 Hz), clash aim so blocks meet the cut, hit-stop body time, sparks, smear ribbon, ink impact frame, auto sound cues (whoosh/clash/scrape) → `output/<film>.events.json`

systems.name: Combat layer (shared)
systems.does: The fight layer of both preview engines, in one module: blade contact detection (240 Hz segment distance, speed and gap thresholds), clash aim (`clashes`), hit-stop body time (`bodyT`/`filmT`; in `main.js` the shots, rigs and authored action times run on body time), smear ribbon, paper sparks + flash light, ink silhouette impact frame, camera punch, eye glow states + blinks + voice pulse (`cast.<id>.face: "eyes"`), auto sound cues (whoosh, steel clash or wood clap for a bokken, scrape) → `window.EVENTS` → `output/<film>.events.json` → SOUND; FX post stack (`fxBase`/`fx`) with a CA flash and bloom pulse on each contact

systems.name: Studio audit (automated QA)
systems.does: Runs on any film without drawing it: per-frame camera, joints on screen, lines of sight, foreground blockers, lens in geometry / under ground, pops, foot slide, blade teleports, smear, dead holds, 180° line, cut rhythm, slow-motion share, hook; pixel checks (black, burnt-out, flat); sound checks (hit has a transient, 9 dB over the whoosh, mush, loudness, stale mix). Scored report, exit 1 on a critical finding. Pages expose `window.AUDIT` through `engine/audit-hooks.js`

systems.name: Studio standard
systems.does: The rules every video must pass, taste + numbers; effects are light, characters are paper; beat → camera table; timing tables; the gate before a render

systems.name: Ground FX + afterimages
systems.does: From the motion alone: dash kick-up, wake line, skid spray, take-off and landing rings of sand, contact shadow pools, afterimages of light, and their sound cues (`dash-burst`, `skid-dust`, `jump-push`, `land-thud`)
systems.status_note: ✅ (motion page: on by default; main engine: opt-in `effects.ground`, `effects.contactShadow`)

systems.name: Cinematographer camera (motion page)
systems.does: `cameraOpts.solver: 2` (subject-relative spring, hard cuts, in-frame / ground / prop guards) + the `compose` framing solver (screen position, size, lead room, orbit, crane, push-in, dolly-zoom) + speed ramps `film.ramps` (film → world → body clocks)

systems.name: Synthesised sword sounds
systems.does: Our own layered clash (tink + ring + body + paper crinkle), light clash, scrape, 3 whooshes, draw shing; no licence needed

systems.name: Earshot sound bank (existing tool)
systems.does: 252 code-made sound effects (MIT, github.com/Leonxlnx/earshot), each whoosh aimed so its loudest moment lands on the blade's fastest frame; cues use `"earshot": "<id>"`, automatic whooshes via `autoSounds.whoosh.earshot`

systems.name: Free model router
systems.does: Sends writing, code, reasoning and image review to free models (Cerebras, NVIDIA Nemotron 550B / vision, Groq, Kimi), with fallback order and a usage log, so Claude usage goes to direction only

systems.name: Free agent worker
systems.does: Runs the free NVIDIA models in a tool loop (read/write/patch/search/run/look) so they do multi-step work at no usage cost; path-sandboxed, command allow-list, protected files

systems.name: OmniRoute gateway
systems.does: Local MIT gateway (github.com/cheaper-inference/OmniRoute) over 400+ models with automatic fallback, so a rate-limited free provider never stops the work; used as the last resort in every `tools/ai.py` chain

systems.name: Blender Skills pack (existing tool)
systems.does: 94 Blender skills for Claude Code (MIT, github.com/arjun988/blender-skills): camera-cinematography, animation, rigging, lighting, lookdev, materials, rendering, compositing, vfx-fx, cloth-sim, historical-worlds, qa-review…

systems.name: Voice (spoken lines)
systems.does: Film `"voice"` lines → Kokoro-82M TTS (Apache-2.0, CPU) → cinematic chain (warmth, compression, hall, inner-monologue) → `output/<film>.voice.json`: cues mixed by SOUND with beds ducked 8 dB, plus 24 fps loudness envelopes to pulse the eyes
systems.status_note: ✅ (wired into main.js and motion.js via fxBase / fx)

systems.name: Paper materials (Blender)
systems.does: Reusable Lantern Origami shaders: faceted washi (true-normal facets, fibre bump, per-facet tone, translucency, inner glow, stripes, sky haze), paper sea, metal

systems.name: Slash effects (Blender)

systems.name: Sets (modular, data-driven, Blender)
systems.does: A location = one JSON in `library/sets/`: kit pieces with positions, sizes and seeds (ishigaki stone walls, plaster walls, kawara roofs, tenshu keep, yaguramon gate, floor planks, tatami, shoji, rooms, torii, toro lanterns, stairs, bridge, bamboo, pine, cherry, rocks, 2.5D paper-cut `layers` backdrops, fog, rain, petals/embers/dust, moon, the Ganryūjima island), lighting presets (night, dusk, dawn, day, overcast), fighter key/fill/rim, camera anchors `CAM_*`, marks `MARK_*`; realistic procedural stone, plaster, wood, tile, lacquer, washi materials; optional origami samurai on the marks in a pose; previews. Sets: castle-courtyard, dojo-interior, bamboo-forest, ganryujima-beach, castle-skyline-2d5

systems.name: Poly Haven layer (CC0 photo textures + HDRI ambient)
systems.does: Search / download / cache CC0 Poly Haven textures (diffuse, normal GL, roughness, displacement, AO) and HDRIs, a role → asset manifest, a triplanar photo-detail layer mixed into the set materials (detail, tint, bump, roughness, AO; facets and washi fibre kept) and an HDRI lighting world (normalised and colour-matched to the procedural sky, sun clamped, camera still sees the procedural sky). On per set with `"polyhaven": true`

systems.name: Modular origami character factory
systems.does: A character = one JSON recipe in `library/character-recipes/`: parts picked from a registry of folded paper pieces (kasa wide/narrow, hachigane, angular/long face masks with eye slits, hair and topknot, layered or plain kimono body with shoulder-to-sternum planes, crossed left-over-right lapels, obi with knot and cord, upper and hanging sleeves as separate folded bags, forearm and kote, folded-finger hands, TWO real pleated hakama legs, tabi+zori or war boots, sode and do lamellar plates, sheathed katana, tassels), each snapped to a socket on the shared humanoid rig (the same joint names as `engine/figure.js` and `rig_trellis.py`, so `library/poses.json` drives it), scaled inside an approved range, dressed from one washi material family with world-scale fibre, rigid parts parented to a bone and flexible ones skinned across 2-3 bones. A second character is made by swapping parts in the recipe only. `part_validator.py` gates the library: material, scale, fibre, pivot, socket, self-intersection, solidify spikes, joint gaps across a five-pose sweep and silhouette readability

systems.name: Blender film render (TRELLIS hero)
systems.does: The owner's reference character fights in Blender from film data: `tools/export_motion.mjs` writes what the preview engine really did per frame (joints, sword, camera, trees, events → `output/<film>.motion.json`); `rig_trellis.py` rigs any TRELLIS `.glb` (our joint names + a table to the standard humanoid names, bone-heat skin with scripted cleanup, relit paper, inner lantern, real-metal katana in a two-hand IK grip, sleeve follow-through) with three drivers: `library/poses.json`, film motion, BVH motion capture; `film_blender.py` renders it with dark cinematic light re-set per frame from the camera, the slash as swept light, dust, tree props, motion blur, and the film's camera or 12 named camera moves / a per-film plan

systems.name: FX post-processing (three.js preview)
systems.does: Deterministic effect stack any page can import: bloom (UnrealBloomPass), one lens pass (colour-grade moods, vignette, film grain, letterbox, chromatic-aberration flash, radial speed lines, ink impact frame, flash/fade), light-shaft cards, seeded particles (dust/ember/petal/snow/ash/shard), glint "ping", trauma shake; `fxAt()` turns film `fx` events into per-frame params; catalogue of 42 effects in `library/effects.json`

systems.name: Architecture (the six modules)
systems.does: The shape of the project: one canonical timeline + Timeline Exporter, Fight Director, Camera Director, Paper Damage Bridge, Render Supervisor, Visual Critic; which code implements each, what is still missing, where a change goes

systems.name: Canonical animation timeline
systems.does: ONE interchange format every renderer reads: per-frame bone world transforms (root motion in bone 0), the weapon at sub-frame resolution, the camera (position, rotation, fov, focal length, focus distance), shots + cut frames, events with stable ids (attack-start, blade-contact, paper-cut, footstep, cue…), lights, effect parameters, asset references, the ONE three.js→Blender coordinate conversion, and a backward-scrub determinism check. Covers motion-page films AND the shots-based main engine

systems.name: Fight Director
systems.does: The fight pipeline as one verification pass over the contact analysis: fighters within weapon reach at each planned clash, the defender's reaction within 0–3 frames of contact, the clash-aim (IK) residual, blade trajectories at 240 Hz (no tunnelling, no teleporting tip) → ONE verified event per strike (`window.EVENTS.strikes`) that drives contact + sound + camera + damage

systems.name: Camera evaluator (Camera Director)
systems.does: Scores every shot against measurable requirements: subject / weapon / target visibility and occlusion, action clarity on the strike frame, framing size vs the size the shot asks for, continuity (180° line, 30° rule), cut timing against the verified events, camera motion (whip without a cut, jerk, clearance from geometry) and emotional fit per beat. Rejects a failure with its reason and proposes the nearest passing alternative from `library/shots.json`; it is also the camera section of the studio audit

systems.name: Paper Damage Bridge
systems.does: The contract between a cut in the film and the paint in the paper: every verified cut → one damage event (part, time, seed, UV window and mm-per-texel for that shot size, gravity, planned wound polyline, KIZU onset / depth / drips) that Blender, the three.js preview and `engine/shimi.py` all read; merged back into the timeline as `damage` events
systems.status_note: 🧪 contract + stub (the UV sweep is planned, not measured)

systems.name: Render Supervisor
systems.does: Renders a film shot by shot from the timeline: one quality-preset table for every renderer (draft / preview / final / hero), retries, per-shot failure isolation and resume from `output/<film>.render-state.json` (a frame hash per shot, so a timeline change re-renders only what changed)

systems.name: Unreal export (verified FBX)
systems.does: Our rigged origami character → an Unreal-ready FBX, with Epic's own Send-to-Unreal settings and a round-trip verifier: three files (Skeletal Mesh, an Animation Sequence with root motion, an A-pose retarget source), UE5 Mannequin or Mixamo bone names, and ten checks on a re-import (175 cm scale, Z up, `root` at the origin, root motion in metres, skin weights, baked curves, bone names). Epic's `send2ue` / `ue2rigify` add-ons are installed (MIT) for the live push the day Unreal exists
systems.command: blender -b -t 2 -P blender/character/export_unreal.py -- --model ronin_base --names ue5 --motion output/dash-test.motion.json --f0 0 --f1 48 --out output/unreal/ronin_dash.fbx

systems.name: Outside-tool evaluation
systems.does: Nine third-party tools checked against rule 6 (code AND weights read separately), installed where safe, tested on our own assets, and recorded: Epic BlenderTools (kept), Rigger (GPL, tested, does not beat our rig), FreeMoCap (AGPL, needs 2+ cameras), RGB MoCap (non-commercial models, study only), TRELLIS.2 (MIT weights; nvdiffrast/nvdiffrec are the non-commercial trap), three agent-skill repos, FilmAgent, Fab's five licence pitfalls, Unreal_Tools

systems.name: TRELLIS.2 Kaggle job
systems.does: Image → 3D with Microsoft TRELLIS.2-4B (code MIT, weights MIT) on Kaggle's free T4, built like `gpu/kaggle_trellis/`: own Python 3.10 + torch 2.6/cu124, xformers (a T4 is sm_75, so no flash-attn and no native bf16), FlexGEMM + CuMesh + o-voxel, GLB export through `o_voxel.postprocess.to_glb`. It deliberately does not install nvdiffrast or nvdiffrec (NVIDIA Source Code Licence, non-commercial) and writes no preview video — the neutral-light clay renders that compare a generation against TRELLIS v1 are done in Blender with `clay_compare.py`
